obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule (GLBA)
basis: 16 CFR 314.2(h)(2)(viii) names an accountant or other tax preparation service in the business of completing income tax returns as a financial institution, and individual tax clients have a customer relationship (314.2(e)(2)(i)(H)). The firm completes about 420,000 individual returns a year and holds records on about 2.9 million consumers, so the 314.6 exception (fewer than 5,000 consumers) does not apply and every 314.4 element applies. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: IRC 7216 preparer disclosure and use limits
basis: The firm and every employee who helps prepare returns are tax return preparers (301.7216-1(b)(2)); disclosures to lenders, the offshore provider and AI services need a permission or a prior written consent

obligation: IRS e-file, PTIN and WISP expectations
basis: Authorized IRS e-file Provider (ERO) with 30 EFINs and about 5,200 PTIN holders: Pub. 1345 incident reporting, signature and retention duties and the Form W-12 acknowledgment apply. Pub. 4557 and Pub. 5708 are guidance; the legal WISP duty comes from 16 CFR 314

obligation: FAR Basic Safeguarding clause
applies: Yes, for the government services practice
basis: About 30 federal civilian contracts include the clause; it applies to the systems that hold Federal Contract Information, not to the TEP. Awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation carry the same requirements as FAR 52.240-93

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 and CMMC
basis: No DoD contracts and no CUI clauses in the contract register; engagement acceptance declines work that would require them. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: HIPAA as business associate
applies: Yes, for PHI held for about 240 health care clients
basis: The firm creates, receives or maintains PHI for covered entities in audit and consulting engagements, so it is a business associate (45 CFR 160.103) subject to the Security Rule (164.302), breach notice to covered entities (164.410) and the agreement limits (164.502(a)(3)). The PHI sits in the audit platform and consulting data rooms, not the TEP. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: ABA Model Rules 1.1 and 1.6(c) as adopted in Florida
citation: Rules Regulating The Florida Bar, Rules 4-1.1 and 4-1.6(e)
basis: The firm does not practice law. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: AICPA Code of Professional Conduct, confidential client information
basis: A professional standard, not law, incorporated through state boards of accountancy; the firm is a licensed CPA firm. Noted in P03; its text was not verified from the source

obligation: CIRCIA (proposed)
basis: Final rule not published at intake; counsel's memo lists it as proposed. Reporting to CISA is voluntary until it takes effect. Rechecked in P03 and P08

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (worked example)
basis: The firm holds personal information of Florida residents at its 12 Florida offices; Florida is the worked example for state law

obligation: Breach notification and data security laws of other states
citation: Statutes of each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Offices in 14 states and clients in all 50 states; notify under the law of each state of residence, using counsel's state matrix

obligation: Florida Digital Bill of Rights
basis: A controller must exceed $1 billion in global gross annual revenue and meet one of three business tests (online advertising revenue, a smart speaker service, or an app store). The firm passes the revenue test and meets none of the three. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: Comprehensive state consumer privacy laws, including the California CPPA ADMT rules
citation: State consumer privacy statutes and regulations
basis: Tracked by the Office of General Counsel in the firm's state privacy program, outside these deliverables
analyzed_in: Office of General Counsel; P10 (noted for AI-010)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (the firm itself)
basis: The firm is a private partnership owned by its CPA partners, not an SEC registrant. Its SEC-registrant clients must assess incidents on third-party systems they use, which drives the client-notice step in P08. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 (the firm itself)
basis: Same: the firm is not a registrant

obligation: FAR clauses on covered telecommunications, Kaspersky and FASCSA articles
applies: Yes, for the government services contracts
basis: The about 30 federal contracts include FAR 52.204-23 and 52.204-25; FASCSA reporting applies only where the clause is in a contract

obligation: Client contract notice and assurance terms (SEC-registrant clients, SL-1, SL-2, advisory)
basis: Notice terms of 24 to 72 hours for SEC-registrant clients; SL-1 agreements require deletion within 90 days and an annual SOC 2 Type 2 report; SL-2 agreements set 99.5% availability and 24-hour response, and corporate clients ask for a SOC 2 Type 2 report

obligation: Sanctions screening before any extortion payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; the cyber policy also requires insurer approval before any payment

obligation: Cyber and professional liability policy notice conditions
basis: Contractual notice duties to the insurers

obligation: HIPAA duties of the firm's employee health plan
basis: The employee health plan is a separate covered entity handled by the benefits program and is outside these deliverables

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
citation: PCI DSS (contractual through the payment processor)
basis: Client card payments run on the payment processor's hosted page; card data is not entered on firm systems

obligation: PCAOB and professional quality and independence standards
citation: PCAOB rules; AICPA and SEC independence rules
basis: The firm is PCAOB-registered and audits about 140 issuers; audit quality and independence are governed by the quality management system and are outside this security analysis. Independence also bars the firm's SOC practice from examining the firm
